Rerun events on their own, from saved states

Source: R/event_states.R
event_states.Rd

Looking at how a model handles the largest events, while changing its parameters, needs each change to show at once. Rerunning a 15-minute record of sixteen years takes seconds; the events in it are a small part of the record. event_states() runs the record once and saves the model's state at the start of each event's window. run_events() then runs only the windows, from those states.

Usage

event_states(model, forcing, events, state = NULL, lead_h = NULL, tail_h = 12)

run_events(model, forcing, saved, which = NULL)

Arguments

model

A model from pdm_model() or pdm_from_config().

forcing

Forcing as for run_pdm().

events

Events from find_events() on the same record.

state

Starting state of the full run; by default initial_state().

lead_h

Hours before each event (the earlier of its rain and flow starts) at which its window starts.

tail_h

Hours after each event's flow window that its window runs on.

saved

Saved states from event_states().

which

Events to run, by row of events; all by default.

Value

event_states(): a list with first and last (each window's first and last row of the record), states (the state before each window's first row), lead_h, tail_h, events and the model the states were saved from. run_events(): a list with one element per event run, each a list of rows (rows of the record) and q_m3s (simulated flow on those rows).

Details

Same parameters, same answer. With the model the states were saved from, run_events() reproduces the full run exactly.

Changed fast parameters: a lead-in. A saved state belongs to the parameters it was saved with. When the surface stores or the time delay change, the surface store and delay queues at the event's start would be those of the old parameters. So each window starts lead_h hours before its event, and the fast stores settle to the new parameters before the rain arrives. A lead-in five times the sum of the surface time constants is enough: on a 15-minute record, slowing the stores from 6 and 10 hours to 12 and 24 hours left peaks 15% out after a 24-hour lead-in, 2% after 72 hours and 0.02% after 180 hours. run_events() warns when the lead-in is shorter than that. Save with a lead-in long enough for the slowest stores you will try. A time delay that changes the length of the delay queues has its queues resized, with any water past the new end added to the last place.

Changed slow parameters: save again. The soil and groundwater stores are kept from the saved run, and they depend on every other parameter: changing b or cmax moved event peaks by 50 to 130% in the same test, however long the lead-in. run_events() therefore refuses a model that differs from the saved one in anything but the surface stores and the time delay.

The default lead-in is three response times of the catchment, and at least a day.

See also

find_events(), event_scores()

Examples

set.seed(4)
n <- 24 * 120
forcing <- data.frame(rain = ifelse(runif(n) < 0.05, rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 5), 0),
                      pet = 0.05)
model <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 20)
flow <- run_pdm(model, forcing)$output$q_m3s
events <- find_events(forcing$rain, flow, dt = 1)
saved <- event_states(model, forcing, events)
faster <- pdm_model(area_km2 = 20, surface = FlodeCascadeRouting(k1 = 1, k2 = 2))
reruns <- run_events(faster, forcing, saved, which = 1:3)
lengths(lapply(reruns, `[[`, "q_m3s"))
#> [1] 69 47 62
